advice: Base: `existing-sme`, source hash `3719c58530161598ab9a537a43be749a5287c8d8dbd35b855e5afea97cd15258`. Experiment: fuse A transpose and GEMM by producing one 32-row A panel (two adjacent 16-lane FP32 row groups) into ZA, reading the transposed row vectors for the existing four-tile MOPA update, then storing that panel to the full `at[k*n+i]` scratch layout. Keep the outer output-column tile loop and reduction in increasing `k`; for each output row panel, compute its A transpose panel once, then reuse it across all 32-column output tiles. This avoids a separate full-matrix transpose pass while preserving the current four ZA accumulators. For n=512 this repeats transpose work for each row panel only if the panel is regenerated inside the column-tile loop; do not do that. Measure full timed-call work, including allocation and all scratch reads/writes, and report transpose and compute data movement. Hypothesis: panel fusion may reduce separate-pass traffic and improve locality. It is unverified; no gain is established.
risks: The full transposed scratch is still needed to preserve the existing output-column-major compute schedule, so fusion may add complexity without removing scratch traffic. Repeating the transpose for each output-column tile would multiply transpose work by 16 and likely erase any benefit. ZA resources conflict: transposing into ZA then using four ZA accumulators requires completing/storing the transpose panel before MOPA, which may limit fusion or force an alternate SVE/register transfer. General odd tails and partial panels need guarded loads/stores, and the transpose must not change FP32 GEMM arithmetic or tolerance.
